title: kith-peer: MAX_BODY_BYTES enforced by byte length not char count — spec says maxBodyBytes
description: DeliverHandler checks msg.body.len() > MAX_BODY_BYTES (line 140) where len() is byte length. The architecture doc defines maxBodyBytes=65536 in the session capability object. A UTF-8 message where each codepoint is 3-4 bytes will be rejected at ~16K-21K characters even though it is within any reasonable character-count interpretation. More critically, a peer could craft a body that is exactly 65536 single-byte ASCII chars but whose JSON encoding is larger. Bytes is the right unit only if the spec says bytes — the name 'maxBodyBytes' is consistent with bytes — but the intent should be documented, and the check is applied after serde has already decoded the JSON string, so the byte count is of the decoded UTF-8, not the wire bytes, which is arguably correct. Flag: intent and unit need explicit documentation.
